items.title: Hayley Williams’ Duo Power Snatch Release EP2
items.summary:
Hayley Williams and producer Daniel James released EP2, the second collection of songs from their duo Power Snatch, posting it to Bandcamp with no advance announcement. The pair formed the project at the start of the year and put out EP1, also a Bandcamp exclusive, within days of announcing it.

The gap between the two releases has not been quiet. Power Snatch covered This Is Lorelei, shared new music through an Instagram post, and recorded a pair of songs with the London artist Tiberius b before dropping the new EP.

Stereogum, which reported the release, described hearing the record for the first time while writing about it and offered first impressions rather than a verdict, noting that the opening two tracks lean further into trip-hop than expected and that the track Born Dead sounded close enough to prompt a second check that it was not another This Is Lorelei cover. The site also credited Williams with finding a DIY presentation that keeps her charisma intact.

The timing appears tied to the solar eclipse, based on Williams' eclipse-related Instagram stories and her most recent Substack post. "a struggle to blog because the only thing i want to give away lately is music," she wrote there, adding that "awe is really a power fuel and we do need more more more of that."

EP2 is streaming on Bandcamp now, following the same no-warning, platform-specific pattern as the duo's first release.

items.title: Ritchie Blackmore Performs With Deep Purple for First Time Since Acrimonious Split in Early ’90s, After Warning Fans: ‘I Have Not Played Rock Music in 25 Years’
items.summary:
Ritchie Blackmore joined Deep Purple on stage Wednesday night at Jones Beach in New York, playing with the band he co-founded for the first time since he left it in 1993. The 81-year-old guitarist came out near the end of the set for a single song, "Smoke on the Water."

The appearance was not quite a surprise. As Variety reported, Blackmore gave away the plan the night before during a livestream conversation with his wife, singer Candice Night, saying he wanted fans who had waited decades for the moment to have a chance to get to New York in time. "it is a secret and i don't want anybody to know, but I'm probably going to go up and do an encore with the band, Deep Purple," he said, before joking that the news would surely be kept quiet.

Blackmore said he initiated the reunion himself, sending a message to singer Ian Gillan in Portugal proposing a single encore with "No pressure, just kind of old times sake." Gillan took it to the band and got a thumbs up. Gillan told the Jones Beach crowd that he had received a message from "a local lad" asking to jam, then thanked "the founding member, the great legend, the immortal Ritchie Blackmore."

The estrangement had been thorough. Blackmore, who co-founded the band in 1968, skipped Deep Purple's Rock and Roll Hall of Fame induction in 2016 after being told the touring lineup — which still includes Gillan, drummer Ian Paice and bassist Roger Glover — would not perform with him under any circumstances.

Blackmore was candid about his readiness. "I haven't played rock in 25 years," he said, explaining that he has spent that time on acoustic guitar with Blackmore's Night, the folk-rock band Night fronts, and that he changed the strings on his Strat for the first time in over 25 years. He also described taking a steroid injection in his lumbar area for four herniated discs, and keeping a stool on stage in case he needed it.

Fans outside the venue tracked the show online, with Perrin Wolfson and Jimmy Kay of the Metal Voice podcast livestreaming as photos and video came out from inside. "I feel like we just walked on the moon," they said on getting confirmation the song was underway.

items.title: BTS’ V Reveals Hearing Loss Amid World Tour
items.summary:
BTS member V told fans during a livestream on Wednesday that he is being treated for hearing loss in his right ear, which he said now works at roughly a third of the level of his left. He said he brushed the problem off at first, treating it as a matter of mental strength, and is now on medication and attending regular hospital appointments.

V, whose given name is Kim Tae-hyung, said the hearing problems got worse during his military service. He enlisted in 2023 and was discharged in June 2025, part of the mandatory 18-month service South Korea requires of nearly all able-bodied men. All seven BTS members completed it, beginning with enlistments in 2022.

BBC News, which reported the disclosure, noted that it came midway through the group's Arirang World Tour. The run opened in South Korea in April and marked the first time in years all seven members had performed together. The livestream followed dates in Baltimore, with Los Angeles, Buenos Aires, Bangkok, Sydney and Hong Kong still ahead.

Jungkook joined the same livestream and described a shin injury he has been managing on the road, saying he is close to a stress fracture and will have to be careful to keep performing.

The tour has run alongside a public disagreement with the Recording Academy. In July, BTS said they would not submit music for consideration at the 69th Grammy Awards after the Academy introduced a Best Asian Pop Music Performance category. Grammy CEO Harvey Mason jr. defended the addition, saying it was created "to celebrate the depth, diversity and extraordinary growth of pop artistry coming out of Asia" and that "it's never to divide, but to expand who is recognized by our 15,000 Grammy voters."

items.title: Lauryn Hill and Wyclef Jean Lead 2026 Global Citizen Festival Lineup
items.summary:
Global Citizen Festival returns to the Great Lawn in Central Park on Saturday, Sept. 26, with Lauryn Hill and Wyclef Jean headlining a bill that also includes Lenny Kravitz, John Legend, Lainey Wilson, Shaboozey and Tomorrow x Together. Hugh Jackman hosts, with Rachel Brosnahan and Gayle King also appearing.

Hill and Jean will mark an anniversary of The Score, the second and final Fugees album, which produced "Ready or Not," "Fu-Gee-La" and the group's cover of Roberta Flack's "Killing Me Softly." As Rolling Stone noted, the three original members celebrated the record's 25th anniversary in 2021 and announced a tour that never fully materialized. Third member Pras Michel has since begun a 14-year prison sentence on money laundering, illegal lobbying and campaign finance charges.

The free festival is tied to a campaign focused on getting more children into school, supporting farmers feeding their communities, and expanding access to electricity for millions of people worldwide.

"It's time to gather once again on the Great Lawn, in the middle of New York City, to tell the world an end to extreme poverty is possible," Jackman said in a statement, pointing fans toward the event's points-based advocacy system. Wilson, performing at the festival for the first time, said she was proud to join a lineup supporting "children's education, farmers and food security, and access to electricity."

Tickets come through a free lottery or, alternately, a $25 charitable donation that grants entry immediately.

items.title: The Harrigans Spiral Out Of Control In ‘MobLand’ Season 2 Trailer
items.summary:
Paramount+ released the official trailer for the second season of MobLand, which premieres Sept. 18. The crime drama, helmed by Guy Ritchie, returns with Tom Hardy as fixer Harry Da Souza, Pierce Brosnan as London underworld boss Conrad Harrigan and Helen Mirren as his wife, Maeve.

The new season turns on the Harrigan family coming apart. "May I speak plainly?" Harry asks Conrad in the trailer. "This family is in a death spiral." War is brewing as Conrad's decline turns his son Kevin (Paddy Considine) against him, while cartel operator Kat McAllister (Janet McTeer) circles the family, a new rival played by Johnny Flynn warns that "the fairytale's over," and corrupt retired detective Colin Tattershall (Toby Jones) reports "an exciting development" to a contact.

Joanne Froggatt, Lara Pulver, Anson Boon, Mandeep Dhillon, Jasmine Jobson, Teddie Allen, Emmett J. Scanlan and Ophelia Lovibond also appear in Season 2.

The production had trouble of its own. As Deadline reported, Hardy initially walked away from the show, reportedly over friction with producers and showrunner and writer Jez Butterworth, before returning once the issues were settled.

The ten-episode season rolls out weekly on Fridays through Nov. 20. Ahead of that, Paramount is making Season 1 available free on the Paramount+ Free Content Hub starting Aug. 18, then on Pluto TV and Paramount+ channels on Amazon, Apple and Roku from Aug. 31, with the Paramount+ YouTube channel carrying it until Sept. 30. The series is a Paramount+ commission produced in association with Paramount Television Studios and 101 Studios.
